Description / What Changed: Prompt fix: Likely Cause field now requires citing the EXACT evidence numbers (function code, rate ratio, etc.) instead of vague wording like 'elevated packet rate' - added a GOOD/BAD example pair with concrete numbers (function code 40, 7.7x) to the prompt. User-reported issue: qwen3:8b's Likely Cause text was too generic despite the exact baseline/observed numbers already being in the prompt data.
Models Tested: phi4-mini, qwen3:4b, gemma4:e4b, qwen3:8b, deepseek-r1:8b, gemma4:12b, qwen3:14b
Result Summary: 6/7 models unaffected. REGRESSION FOUND: phi4-mini copy-pasted the GOOD example's literal numbers ("function code 40 ... 7.7x") verbatim in 9/22 calls (8 on the WRONG attack, real data differed), qwen3:8b did it 4/22 times (3 wrong) - small models pattern-matched the example instead of reading the real packet data. qwen3:4b format_compliance dropped further to 9.1% (longer prompt gave it more room to ramble); deepseek-r1:8b avg_completion_tokens jumped to 1620 (was ~450) but stayed 100% compliant. Root-caused and fixed same day in XAI-13 (see below) by replacing the concrete example numbers with text placeholders.
